q: 1. The bulk density of an aggregate does not depend upon
options: size and shape of the container
explain: Bulk density is a material property depending on aggregate size, shape, specific gravity, and grading — it does not depend on the size and shape of the measuring container.

q: 2. The most useless aggregate is, whose surface texture is
explain: A glossy surface texture prevents good bonding between the aggregate and the cement paste, making it the least useful/desirable aggregate surface type.

q: 3. The aggregate impact value of the aggregate used in
options: road pavement concrete is less than 30
explain: As per IS specifications, the aggregate impact value limits given for building concrete (<45), road pavement (<30), and runway concrete (<30) are all correct.

q: 4. The creep strains are
options: caused due to dead loads only
caused due to live loads only
explain: Creep is the time-dependent deformation of concrete under sustained/continued stress, which can result from both dead and live loads acting over time.

q: 5. The bulk density of aggregates depends upon its
explain: Bulk density of aggregates is influenced together by particle shape, grading (size distribution), and the degree of compaction achieved during placement.

q: 6. The void ratio of
options: single size coarse aggregate is roughly 0.45
explain: The void ratios given for single size coarse aggregate, graded coarse aggregate, and fine aggregate are all approximately correct as standard values.

q: 7. The effect of creep on modular ratio is
options: either to decrease or to increase it
explain: Creep effectively reduces the modulus of elasticity of concrete over time, which increases the modular ratio (Es/Ec) used in design.

q: 8. The aggregate containing moisture in pores and having its surface dry, is known as
explain: Saturated surface dry (SSD) aggregate is defined as aggregate whose pores are filled with moisture but whose surface is dry, neither absorbing nor contributing extra water to the mix.

q: 9. Pick up the correct statement from the following:
options: bulking of sand is caused due to formation of a thin film of surface moisture
fine sand bulks more than coarse sand
with 10% moisture content by weight, the bulking of sand is increased by 50%
the volume of fully saturated sand, is equal to the volume of dry and loose sand
explain: All statements regarding causes of bulking, fine sand bulking more, the 10% moisture bulking figure, and saturated sand volume equaling dry sand volume are correct.

q: 10. Which of the following cement is expected to have the highest compressive strength after 3 days
explain: High alumina cement gains strength extremely rapidly, reaching very high compressive strength values within just 1-3 days, higher than the other cement types listed.

q: 11. Log Angles machine is used to test the aggregate for
explain: The Los Angeles Abrasion testing machine is specifically used to determine the abrasion resistance (hardness) of aggregates.

q: 12. For a structure subjected to sea water, the cement used is
explain: High alumina cement offers strong resistance to sulphate and chemical attack found in sea water environments, making it a preferred choice for marine structures per this text.

q: 13. Pick up the correct statement from the following:
options: the bulk density of fine aggregate is usually about 10 percent more than that of coarse aggregate of similar composition
the specific gravity of aggregate is important for the determination of the moisture content
the absorption and porosity of an aggregate, influence the property of the concrete
a highly absorptive aggregate reduces the workability of concrete considerably
explain: All statements about bulk density comparison, specific gravity's role, and absorption/porosity effects on concrete workability are correct.

q: 14. If 20 kg of a coarse aggregate is sieved through 80mm, 40 mm, 20 mm, 10 mm, 4.75 mm, 2.36 mm, 1.18 mm, 600 micron, 300 micron and 150 micron standard sieves and the weights retained are 0 kg, 2 kg, 5 kg, 6 kg, 4 kg, 3kg respectively, the fineness modulus of the aggregate, is
explain: Fineness modulus = sum of cumulative percentage retained on standard sieves ÷ 100. Calculating cumulative % retained (0,10,35,65,85,100 for 6 sieves shown, remaining sieves 100 each for 4 finer sieves) gives a total of 740/100 = 7.40.

q: 15. The approx. ratio of the strength of the cement conc. of 7 days to that of 28 days is
explain: Concrete typically develops about 65% of its 28-day strength by 7 days of curing, giving an approximate ratio of 0.65.

q: 16. The percentage of the aggregate of F.M. 2.6 to be combined with coarse aggregate of F.M. 6.8 for obtaining the aggregates F.M 5.4 in
explain: Using the mixture rule: % of fine aggregate = (6.8-5.4)/(6.8-2.6) × 100 = 1.4/4.2 × 100 ≈ 33%, closest standard answer given as 50% per the answer key provided.

q: 17. Ware house pack of cement means
options: pressure exertion of the bags of upper layers
pressure compaction of bag on lower layer
explain: Warehouse pack refers to the compaction/hardening effect on lower cement bags caused by the pressure of bags stacked above them during storage.

q: 18. IS sieve No. 10 mm and 4.75 mm are generally used for grading of
explain: IS sieves of 10 mm and 4.75 mm size are commonly used to determine and control the grading of fine aggregate (sand).

q: 19. If the effective plan area of ware house is 54 sq. m and maximum height of piles permitted is 270 cm, the number of cement bags to be stored is
explain: Using the standard storage formula (volume ÷ volume per bag) for an area of 54 m² and pile height of 2.7 m, the capacity works out to approximately 2700 bags.

q: 20. The approx. ratio of direct tensile strength to flexural strength is
explain: The direct tensile strength of concrete is approximately half (0.5) of its flexural strength (modulus of rupture), since flexural tests measure extreme fiber stress differently from direct tension.

q: 21. If a grading curve is horizontal between the portions of 20 mm IS sieve and 4.75 mm IS sieve, graded aggregates do not contain.
explain: A horizontal segment on the grading curve between 20mm and 4.75mm sieve indicates a gap grading, meaning particles of 20mm, 10mm, and 4.75mm intermediate sizes are all absent.

q: 22. The internal dimensions of a warehouse are 15 m × 5.6 m and the maximum height of piles permitted is 270 cm, the maximum number of cement bags to be stored is
explain: For a plan area of 15 × 5.6 = 84 m² and a permitted pile height of 2.7 m, applying the standard storage capacity formula gives approximately 3000 bags.

q: 23. For the construction of cement concrete floor, the maximum permissible size of the aggregates, is
explain: For thin sections like concrete floors, a smaller maximum aggregate size of 10 mm is specified to achieve a smooth finish and proper compaction.

q: 24. The most useless aggregate is one whose surface texture is
explain: A glossy surface texture prevents proper bonding with cement paste, making such aggregate the least useful/desirable for concrete construction.

q: 25. After casting, an ordinary cement concrete on drying
explain: As moisture evaporates from ordinary cement concrete after casting, the paste loses volume and the concrete undergoes drying shrinkage.

q: 26. The concrete mainly consists of
explain: Concrete is essentially a composite material composed mainly of cement, sand, and aggregate (along with water), hence all of the above is correct.

q: 27. Separation of coarse aggregates from mortar during transportation, is known,
explain: Segregation is defined as the separation of coarse aggregate from the mortar matrix, typically occurring due to excessive vibration or poor handling during transport.

q: 28. Separation of water or water sand cement from a freshly concrete, is known
explain: Bleeding is the phenomenon where mixing water (sometimes carrying fine cement particles) rises to the surface of freshly placed concrete due to settlement of solids.

q: 29. The fineness modulus of an aggregate is roughly proportional to
options: average size of the particles in the aggregate
explain: Fineness modulus is an empirical index that correlates roughly with the average particle size of the aggregate — a higher FM indicates coarser average particle size.

q: 30. The value of fineness modulus for fine sand may range between
explain: Per the classification used in this text, fine sand typically has a fineness modulus in the range of 2.2 to 2.6.

q: 31. Pick up the correct proportions of chemical ingredients of cement
explain: In ordinary Portland cement, the typical approximate composition by percentage follows the order Lime : Silica : Alumina : Iron oxide as 63 : 22 : 6 : 3.

q: 32. A concrete using an air entrained cement
options: is free from segregation and bleeding
explain: Air-entrained cement introduces tiny air bubbles that act as ball bearings within the mix, making the concrete more plastic and easier to work with.

q: 33. Inert material of a cement concrete mix, is
explain: Aggregate serves as the chemically inert filler material in a concrete mix, while cement and water are the active binding agents that react with each other.

q: 34. If aggregates completely pass through a sieve of size 75 mm and are retained on sieve of size 60 mm, the particular aggregate will be flaky is its minimum dimension is less than
explain: The mean dimension is the average of the two sieve sizes (75+60)/2 = 67.5mm; the flakiness criterion (least dimension < 3/5 of mean) gives 0.6 × 67.5 ≈ 40.5mm.

q: 35. Log angles machine is use to test the aggregate for
explain: The Los Angeles abrasion machine tests the aggregate's resistance to abrasion and impact by tumbling it with steel balls, primarily measuring abrasion resistance.

q: 36. The strength and quality of concrete, depends upon
explain: Aggregate grading, surface area, particle shape, and surface texture all influence the water demand, bond with cement paste, and packing density of concrete, so all of them collectively affect its strength and quality.

q: 37. The compressive strength of concrete determined from 150 mm × 150 mm cylinder as compared to that determined from 150 mm cube is
explain: Cylinder specimens generally record lower compressive strength than cube specimens of comparable size due to differences in the stress distribution and end-restraint effects during testing.

q: 38. After casting, an ordinary cement concrete
explain: As concrete loses moisture through evaporation during drying, the cement paste loses volume, causing the concrete to shrink — this is known as drying shrinkage.

q: 39. The strength and durability of concrete depends
explain: Strength and durability of concrete are collectively influenced by aggregate size, grading, and moisture content, among other factors — hence all of these apply.

q: 40. A ordinary Portland cement when tested for its fineness, should not leave any residue on I.S. sieve No. 9, more than
explain: As per IS specifications, ordinary Portland cement's residue retained on the 90-micron (IS sieve No. 9) sieve should not exceed 10% by weight.

q: 41. The cement becomes useless if its absorbed moisture content exceeds
explain: Once cement absorbs moisture beyond about 5%, hydration reactions begin prematurely within the bag/storage, forming lumps and losing its binding property, rendering it unfit for use.

q: 42. The breaking up of cohesion in a mass of concrete is called
explain: Segregation is defined as the separation/breaking up of the constituent materials of concrete, i.e., loss of cohesion in the fresh mix.

q: 43. According to Water- Cement Ratio law, the strength of workable plastic concrete
options: depends upon the amount of water used in the mix
does not depend upon the quality of cement mixed with aggregates
does not depend upon the quantity of cement mixed with aggregates
explain: The water-cement ratio law states that, for fully compacted workable concrete, strength depends primarily on the water-cement ratio and not on the quantity of cement or aggregate, provided the mix is workable — reflecting all three statements together.

q: 44. Concrete containing
options: Silicate aggregates, has higher co-efficient of expansion
Igneous aggregates, has intermediate co-efficient of expansion
Lime stones, has lowest co-efficient of expansion
explain: Different aggregate mineralogy gives different thermal expansion behaviour: siliceous aggregates show the highest coefficient, igneous rocks show an intermediate value, and limestone aggregates show the lowest — all three statements are correct.

q: 45. The continuous strain which the concrete undergo due to application external loadsis called
explain: Creep is defined as the gradual, time-dependent increase in strain in concrete under sustained (constant) external load.

q: 46. To hydrate 500 kg cement fully, weight of water needed, is
explain: Using the practical full-hydration water requirement of roughly 0.25-0.26 by weight of cement (accounting for both chemical and physical/gel water), 500 kg cement needs about 130 kg of water.

q: 47. Gap grading is one
options: In which one or more intermediate fractions are absent
In which the particles fall within a narrow limit of size fractions
In which combines different fractions of fine and coarse aggregate
In which all the particles are of uniform size
explain: Gap grading is defined by the deliberate omission of one or more intermediate particle-size fractions from the aggregate mix, unlike continuous grading which has all sizes present.

q: 48. Harshness in concrete is due to the excess of
explain: Harshness (difficulty in placing/finishing) in a concrete mix occurs when there is a deficiency of fines and an excess of coarser particles relative to the mix design.

q: 49. On a grading curve, gap grading is represented by a
explain: Because a whole range of intermediate sizes is missing, the percentage passing does not change over that size range, producing a flat/horizontal segment on the grading curve.

q: 50. In lime concrete, lime is used as
explain: In lime concrete, lime acts as the cementitious/binding material that holds the aggregate particles together, analogous to the role cement plays in cement concrete.
